items.title: Urbie Green interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 29, 1995
items.q: Or, “Jack Teagarden I wrote this for.”

ctx.x: When I listen to music behind some commercials these days I’m thinking, you know, people had to actually play this. And someone sat down and wrote this thing. And I’m wondering sometimes how some of the players keep a straight face.

Well in the studio sometimes you get in a situation where you kind of have to be an actor, like you’re not really playing yourself, when you’re choosing — I mean I’m talking about musical acting. Like they’d say, “play this like Tommy Dorsey,” or you know, so you’d try to play, there was only one Tommy Dorsey, so you do something similar to that. Or, “Jack Teagarden I wrote this for.” One time I had to imitate a dog eating dog food [scats]. I guess that’s really, what’s I can’t think, I’ve got a small vocabulary.…

Well we’ve had some interesting talk about what people learn in college as opposed to what happens out in the real world you know. And nowadays I know you’ve done work in colleges with the music programs. What happens after they get out of school, you know? Have you ever talked to students after they got out and any insight into —
